title: K-flatness of the finite ringed Koszul dual tower
statement: ∀ m : ℕ, CochainComplex.IsAcyclicTensorKFlat ((ringedKoszulDualTower O r b).obj (op m))

proof.text: For a bicomplex supported in rows 0 and 1, construct an isomorphism from its degree-n total term to the biproduct of the (0,n) and (1,n-1) terms. Use totalDesc and the two total inclusions; total hom-ext and biproduct hom-ext prove the inverse identities. Apply this to a positive Koszul factor tensor P and use its degree-zero and degree-one identifications with the tensor unit. Thus the new term is P^n direct sum P^(n-1). Induction on r, starting with O[0], proves that every positive Koszul term is finite free and that all negative-degree terms vanish. The finite basis at the inductive step is the disjoint union of the two preceding finite bases.

Use the specified product-limit projections of the Hom complex. In Hom(P,O[0])^n every factor except p=-n is zero, since the target single complex vanishes in degree p+n. Reuse fan_projection_isIso and homObj_isZero_right from Sheaf.Algebra.Homology.FiniteFreeZeroHomologyEvaluationIso (available through a proof-only import all). The former proves that the surviving projection is invertible by a limit lift with identity at -n and zero elsewhere; the latter proves that internal Hom into a zero target vanishes. This gives Hom(P,O[0])^n isomorphic to the internal Hom from P^(-n) to O. Transport a finite-free basis of P^(-n) through homFunctor and apply the source-library homObjFreeUnitIso. Therefore every dual term is finite free. In positive degree it is zero, since P^(-n) is zero.

The tensor unit is flat. Apply ObjectProperty.flat_coproduct to the finite family of unit modules defining each free module, then transport flatness along the constructed term isomorphisms and take the tensorRight clause, which is SheafOfModules.IsFlat. The dual complex is bounded above by zero, so isKFlat_of_boundedAbove_flat proves the result for each tower index m.
